co_san_juans.blurb: The San Juans are a high, rugged range in southwest Colorado, centered on Ouray, Telluride and Silverton, with many peaks above 13,000 feet. Climbing here is mostly alpine: rock routes on summit faces, snow couloirs, scrambles and winter ice, with a few boulders. The rock is notoriously chossy, protection can be poor, and approaches are long, so technical grades are often modest while the seriousness is high. Backcountry ice generally forms from early December through late March, ranging from moderate to steep WI6 on mixed ground. Larger sub-ranges include the Cimarron Mountains, the Needles, the Grenadiers and the Sneffels Range. Outside the popular hiking peaks, you are unlikely to meet other parties.

nv_willow_spring.blurb: Willow Spring is a sandstone area on the scenic loop at Red Rocks, outside Las Vegas. Single-pitch trad dominates, with a few bolted lines, top-ropes and some multi-pitch on the tier above Lost Creek. Grades run from easy 5.4 and 5.5 climbs up to about 5.12, but the heart of it is 5.6 through 5.10, which makes it a good place for moderate leads. Approaches are generally short. Many climbs are shaded for much of the year, so it works well early in the season or to dodge summer heat. Ragged Edges Area gets morning sun, Mossy Ledges Area is mostly shady, and The Case Face is another large wall. The sandstone is fragile when wet, so wait for it to dry.

on_rattlesnake_point.blurb: Rattlesnake Point sits on the Niagara Escarpment near Milton, Ontario, roughly 45 minutes west of Toronto. The cliffs are jagged limestone, known for caves and scenic edges, with wide views over Nassagaweya Canyon. Traditional leads are the most common, with a good number of sport routes along the western edge and a few top-ropes. Grades start at the easy end and build steadily, with most climbs between 5.6 and 5.10 and a few harder ones, so it suits beginners and intermediate climbers well. The main cliff sectors are the West Cliff, Buffalo Crag, the East Cliff and Bottle Glass.

ut_kane_springs_canyon.blurb: Kane Springs Canyon lies just outside Moab in southeast Utah and holds sandstone climbing of several kinds: mostly trad, plus some sport, aid and a good set of boulder problems. Ice Cream Parlor, the largest wall, is made of good Wingate sandstone and faces west, so it stays cool in the afternoon and works on hot mornings. Routes run from easy 5.5 slabs through a strong core of 5.9 to 5.11 to a handful of 5.12 and 5.13 lines, and boulders are mostly V0 to V6. Invert Offwidth Boulder Circuit and Abraxas Wall are other larger sectors. Summer temperatures can pass 100 degrees, and wet sandstone damages easily, so stay off after rain.

va_mcafee_s_knob.blurb: McAfee's Knob is a bouldering area in southwest Virginia, with blocks along the Appalachian Trail and near the road below. The stone is mostly gritty sandstone, with some smooth patches and hard, slick quartzite. Summit boulders are vertical and rectangular, often 10 to 20 feet tall, with a few roofs and low topouts, and holds range from crimps and slopers to big jugs. Problems run from V0 up to a few at V8 and V9, with most between V0 and V5. Belly Boulder Area, The Corridor and Beyond and Roadside are among the biggest groupings. Cooler months, especially late fall, are best; summer is hot and buggy and some summit boulders grow lichen.

wv_summersville_lake_main.blurb: Summersville Lake is a lakeside cliff area near Summersville, West Virginia, on Nuttall sandstone, the same stone as the New River Gorge. Sport climbing dominates, with trad lines and some boulders. The rock is steep, often overhanging, and features pockets, huecos, slopers and edges, in walls from about 30 to 100 feet tall. Grades range from the 5.8 range to a few at 5.14, with a thick middle from 5.10 to 5.12. Much of the stone faces south, so it suits cool weather, and the water level shapes access: more crags open as the lake drops in autumn. Orange Oswald Wall, Circus Wall, The Long Wall and Pirate's Cove are among the larger sectors.
